name: Multiple System Atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Movement Disorder Society Criteria for MSA (2022 Revision)

criteria.description: Autonomic failure: orthostatic hypotension (>=20/10 mmHg within 3 min standing) or urogenital dysfunction (urinary incontinence or erectile dysfunction in males)
Parkinsonism poorly responsive to levodopa (MSA-P subtype)
Cerebellar ataxia with gait and limb ataxia, cerebellar dysarthria, cerebellar oculomotor dysfunction (MSA-C subtype)
MRI showing putaminal atrophy, hot cross bun sign, or cerebellar/pontine atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Autonomic failure plus poorly levodopa-responsive parkinsonism OR cerebellar ataxia. Clinically established MSA requires additional supportive features.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definite diagnosis requires neuropathological confirmation with alpha-synuclein-positive glial cytoplasmic inclusions.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Combined severe autonomic failure with parkinsonism or cerebellar ataxia
pathognomonic.notes: The combination is the hallmark; individual features are not pathognomonic alone

common.notes: Often earliest autonomic symptom in males

laboratory: No specific blood biomarkers; normal routine labs
Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay (SAA) may be positive in CSF
imaging: MRI: putaminal atrophy with slit-like hyperintensity on T2 (MSA-P)
MRI: hot cross bun sign in pons (MSA-C)
FDG-PET: hypometabolism in putamen, cerebellum, brainstem
Cardiac MIBG: may be normal (unlike Parkinson disease)
genetic: COQ2 mutations reported in familial MSA (rare)
other: Autonomic function testing: severe cardiovascular and sudomotor failure
Urodynamic studies: detrusor hyperreflexia, open bladder neck
EMG: possible denervation of external urethral sphincter (Onuf nucleus)

distinguishingFeatures: Parkinson disease typically responds well to levodopa
MSA has earlier and more severe autonomic failure
Cardiac MIBG is abnormal in PD but often normal in MSA
PAF lacks cerebellar or parkinsonian motor features
PAF has a more benign course
PSP has supranuclear vertical gaze palsy
PSP typically has axial rigidity and backward falls

redFlags: Rapid progression of parkinsonism poorly responsive to levodopa
Early and severe autonomic failure within first few years of motor onset
Stridor or nocturnal laryngeal spasm (risk of sudden death)
references: Gilman S, et al. Second consensus statement on the diagnosis of multiple system atrophy. Neurology. 2008;71(9):670-676.
Wenning GK, et al. The Movement Disorder Society Criteria for the Diagnosis of Multiple System Atrophy. Mov Disord. 2022;37(6):1131-1148.
Fanciulli A, Wenning GK. Multiple-system atrophy. N Engl J Med. 2015;372(3):249-263.
